---
title: Running Training for Cayuga Half Marathon
tags: [running, training, half-marathon, cayuga, injury]
date: 2025-03-15
---

I cannot believe it is already mid-March. The [[Cayuga Half Marathon]] is coming up fast on April 19 and I still feel like I am playing catch-up with my training. The weather has been all over the place lately so most of my weekday runs have been on the treadmill at the gym or quick loops around the neighborhood when it is not pouring. I keep telling myself that consistency matters more than perfect conditions but some days it is hard to get out the door.

My overall plan is pretty straightforward. Long runs on Sundays building from 8 miles up to 12 miles over the next few weeks. I am aiming for a goal time of around 1:55 which would be a big personal record for me on this course. The hills in the second half always sneak up on you so I need to make sure my long runs include some elevation. Last Sunday I did 8.5 miles and felt pretty good until the last mile when my left knee started talking to me again.

The [[left knee pain]] has been an ongoing issue since February. It is not sharp pain exactly, more like a dull ache that shows up after about six or seven miles. I have been foam rolling every night and doing the glute activation exercises that [[Dr. Patel]] recommended back in January. So far it has not gotten worse but I am nervous about pushing the long runs too quickly. Ice after every run seems to help and I have been religious about taking at least one complete rest day during the week.

My shoes are holding up okay. I bought the [[Brooks Ghost 16]] at the beginning of January and they still feel fresh. The cushioning is exactly what my knees need right now. I probably have another 150 miles or so before I should rotate in a new pair but I will wait until after the race to buy them. The bright blue color is starting to look pretty dirty from all the trail sections I have been hitting on weekends.

This week I am supposed to do 10 miles on Sunday if my knee cooperates. I mapped out a route that goes through the park and loops back along the river path. It is mostly flat for the first six miles which should let me focus on keeping an easy pace around 8:45 per mile. My weekday runs are staying in the 4 to 6 mile range with one speed session on Tuesdays. Yesterday I did 6x400m repeats and my legs felt surprisingly springy.

I should probably add some more strength training too. My core has been neglected lately and I know that contributes to the knee issues. Maybe I will try to do the 15-minute routine from the [[Half Marathon Training Plan]] note before work a couple days this week. Nutrition has been decent. I have been making sure to eat enough protein after long runs and I finally remembered to order more electrolytes after running out last weekend.

The race itself is going to be tough but I am excited. [[Sarah]] is running the 5K the same day so at least we can make a morning of it. I need to remember to sign up for the shuttle parking because last year it was a nightmare trying to find a spot near the start. Goal time of 1:55 would put me right around 8:47 pace which feels ambitious but doable if the knee stays quiet and the weather cooperates.

I will update this note after Sunday's long run. For now I am just trying to stay patient and listen to my body. The [[left knee pain]] is the biggest wildcard in all of this. If it flares up badly I may have to adjust the plan and drop one of the longer runs. Better to be safe than sidelined for weeks after the race.

**Next long run target:** 10 miles this Sunday  
**Current weekly mileage:** around 28-32  
**Shoes:** Brooks Ghost 16 (purchased January 2025)  
**Race goal:** 1:55
